_comment: POLICY keys for ~/.claude/settings.json. Applied by bin/apply-settings.sh.
This file is NOT a full copy of settings.json. It holds only the settings that
must be identical on EVERY machine because an instruction file depends on them
being enforced by the harness rather than by Claude remembering to comply.
Everything else in settings.json is legitimately per-machine (installed plugins,
model, theme, marketplaces) and Claude Code rewrites it at runtime, which is why
settings.json is deliberately NOT stowed. See claude-core/.stow-local-ignore.
Adding a key here: only if a rule in claude-core/.claude/instructions/ says the
setting enforces that rule. If it is a preference, it does not belong here.
Merge semantics: objects merge recursively, arrays are UNIONed (policy entries
are guaranteed present, a machine's own additions survive), and this file wins
for any scalar it names.
attribution -> working-style.md, 'No Claude attribution'.
permissions.deny npm/npx -> security.md, 'Never use npm' (supply-chain worm
risk). pnpm and `pnpm dlx` are the sanctioned replacements and are NOT blocked.
Bare and colon-wildcard forms are both listed because a prefix rule like
`Bash(npm:*)` does not match an argument-less `npm`.
hooks.PreToolUse -> working-style.md, 'Never git push origin HEAD, and never
a bare git push. Name the branch.' That rule was an instruction telling Claude
to re-check the branch before pushing, i.e. a control that depends on Claude
remembering, and it failed exactly as written on 2026-08-14: two sessions
shared one checkout, one switched branches, and the other's
main-bound commit landed on that feature branch via `git push origin HEAD`.
Same failure recorded 2026-07-10. Claude Code does NOT detect two interactive
sessions sharing a checkout (verified against the docs 2026-08-14; only
BACKGROUND sessions get an automatic worktree), so nothing upstream catches
this. guard-git-push.sh is the mechanism that replaces the instruction.
It matches the WHOLE command rather than using the hook's `if` key, because
permission rules anchor at the start of the command and the incident began
with `git add`, so `if: Bash(git push *)` would never have fired.
The SECOND PreToolUse hook, guard-repo-collision.sh, supplies the FACT the
push guard cannot: that another session is in this checkout with you. It
warns once per session per repo, on git verbs that WRITE only, and never
blocks. It cannot call SendMessage itself (hooks are shell commands), so it
tells the model to.
hooks.SessionStart -> the policy re-applies itself. Without this, keeping N
machines compliant depends on someone remembering to run this script on each
one, which is the same human-memory dependency that let the old baseline rot.
Chicken-and-egg, stated plainly: the hook cannot install itself, so a NEW
machine still needs one manual `apply-settings.sh` (step 4 of the README's
new-machine list). After that first run the machine is self-correcting.
Companion to the UserPromptSubmit entry; read its _comment for the rationale and
for why the wrapper shape is mandatory. SessionStart surfaces anything left
unacknowledged from a previous session.
peer-ack-hook.sh enforces nothing. It makes an UNANSWERED cross-session message
visible. Claude Code's SendMessage returns success when a message is QUEUED, not
when a peer receives it: a message can sit awaiting approval at the receiving
terminal, expire unread, and leave the sender believing it was delivered.
'Remember which messages are unacknowledged' is a hope, so this is a mechanism.
APPEND-ONLY, do not reorder: apply-settings.sh unions these arrays and collapses
entries sharing a matcher, and execution order within an entry is positional.
The wrapper shape is NOT optional. On UserPromptSubmit both blocking channels
(exit 2 and decision:'block') ERASE the user's prompt outright, and a bash SYNTAX
ERROR exits 2 without executing a single line, so no care inside the script
protects against a bad edit TO it. The trailing 'exit 0' is the only thing that
holds when the file cannot run at all. Covered by tests/test-peer-ack.sh, which
proves both that a broken hook exits 2 and that this wrapper converts it to 0.
Per-machine off switch, outside anything this policy can re-add:
touch "${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/peer-ack/off"
